summary: book-to-skill's headline, 24×–51× fewer tokens than placing the whole book in context to answer one question, comes from tools/discovery_tax.py run on three real books whose texts are not committed (119,264 / 175,253 / 256,287 context-dump tokens vs ~5,000 for book-to-skill, a ~4K core plus ~1K chapter that the tool takes as a design cap unless a generated skill is passed), and the 2.4×–15.6× discovery-loop figures are a model, as the tool's docstring states. Extraction counts, Docling vs pdftotext (164s vs 0.1s; 48 vs 0 tables), a ~$1-per-book generation cost and a one-chapter before/after table are published as results without a committed harness, and docs/performance.md lists 133 auto-detected chapters for Moby-Dick where docs/how-it-works.md lists none. The tools/evals harness for routing and answer accuracy has no live results yet, and docs/research/progressive-disclosure-evals.md summarizes an external study of a book-to-skill-based recipe in which a strong navigator on a single book reduced the accuracy benefit of the pre-built pack.
